paper.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
paper.central_claim: Pretrained skills with learned affordance (value) functions can ground an LLM planner: scoring each skill's language label under the LLM and multiplying by the skill's success probability lets a mobile manipulator execute long-horizon abstract instructions; reported 84% plan / 74% execution success over 101 instructions in a mock kitchen (81%/60% in a real kitchen), nearly doubling non-grounded baselines.

provenance.expectations_hash_reason: no independent expectations file in repo (profile/expectations.json absent); E01-E22 read as transcribed in patterns/main/*.md, covered by domain_cards_hash.overview/conditions
provenance.session_id_reason: subagent cannot read its own session id; no receipt available to the worker
provenance.notes: anchors_version=v2 (3ececdd11cc3d144); phase=production; production-under-anchors-v2, not a frozen rubric; blind seat: sol outputs / aggregate / calibration / archive / old scores not read

sections_read: Appendix A-E incl. Listing 1-3, Tables 5-9, Figures 23-26 captions

status_reason: full text with appendices read; in-scope (frontier LLM scoring frozen learned skills on a real mobile manipulator)

evidence.quote: Grounding the LLM in the real-world via affordances nearly doubles the performance over the non-grounded baselines.
evidence.support_explanation: headline claim (checked against Table 2 in counterevidence)

evidence.quote: The key idea of SayCan is to ground large language models through value functions
evidence.support_explanation: mechanism statement

evidence.quote: This corresponds to multiplying the probability of the language description of the skill given the instruction
evidence.support_explanation: factorization: task-grounding x world-grounding

evidence.quote: In the mock kitchen, PaLM-SayCan achieved a planning success rate of 84% and an execution rate of 74%.
evidence.support_explanation: main result, mock kitchen, 101 instructions

evidence.quote: We find a reduction of planning performance by 3% and execution by 14%
evidence.support_explanation: real kitchen is a drop, not a held-out win

evidence.quote: We ask 3 human raters to indicate whether the plan generated by the model can achieve the instruction, and if 2 out of 3 raters agree that the plan is valid, it is marked a success.
evidence.support_explanation: plan success defined by human majority

evidence.quote: We mark an execution successful if 2 out of 3 raters agree that it is successful.
evidence.support_explanation: execution success by human video raters, majority of three

evidence.quote: achieving 67% and 74% planning success rate respectively
evidence.support_explanation: No VF 67 / Generative 74 vs SayCan 84 plan success; execution of these ablations not run

evidence.quote: where BC NL achieves 0% in all tasks and BC USE achieves 60% for single primitives, but 0% otherwise
evidence.support_explanation: no-LLM policy baselines fail on long-horizon instructions
Table 2 totals: mock plan 84, mock exec 74, kitchen plan 81, exec 60, No VF 67, Gen 74, BC NL 0, BC USE 9

evidence.quote: Overall, 65% of the errors were LLM failures and 35% were affordance failures.
evidence.support_explanation: failure decomposition at plan level

evidence.quote: We test our method in two environments: a real office kitchen and a mock environment mirroring the kitchen, which is also the environment in which the robot
evidence.support_explanation: evaluation environment equals skill-training environment for the mock kitchen

evidence.quote: Since the focus of this work is mainly on planning, we assume the location of objects are known.
evidence.support_explanation: privileged navigation information

evidence.quote: We assume place is always possible
evidence.support_explanation: hand-set place affordance

evidence.quote: The parameters used for calibration are determined empirically.
evidence.support_explanation: affordance calibration is empirical

evidence.quote: involved 17 examples and recovered 88% of the solutions correctly
evidence.support_explanation: prompt tuned in a language-based simulator on 50 instructions

evidence.quote: the system is not easily able to react to situations where individual skills fail despite reporting a high value
evidence.support_explanation: no closed-loop recovery

evidence.quote: To evaluate PaLM-SayCan, we test across 101 instructions from 7 instruction families
evidence.support_explanation: evaluation denominators; family sizes 11-15
PaLM-SayCan vs FLAN-SayCan: plan 84 vs 70, execution 74 vs 61

evidence.quote: SayCan achieved an overall planning success rate of 100% and execution success rate of 33%.
evidence.support_explanation: drawer skills added: execution 33% (21 queries)

evidence.quote: The RL model is trained using 16 TPUv3 chips and for about 100 hours
evidence.support_explanation: only training-side compute disclosed

evidence.quote: but without any additional mechanism to ensure grounding
evidence.support_explanation: closest concurrent neighbor (Huang et al.) described as lacking grounding; corresponds to the Generative baseline
state-dependent instructions: SayCan 64 plan vs No VF 18

evidence.quote: the primary bottleneck of the system is in the range and capabilities of the underlying skills
evidence.support_explanation: author-stated residue

evidence.quote: to the same evaluation protocol in the real kitchen, and then integrated into SayCan
evidence.support_explanation: skills were screened in the real kitchen during development

evidence.quote: we set a cap for the affordances indicating that the skill has been completed and the reward received
evidence.support_explanation: hand-written logic outside Algorithm 1

evidence.quote: If two out of the three raters agree that the skill was accomplished successfully, the episode is labelled with a positive reward.
evidence.support_explanation: skill reward labels also come from human raters

signatures.object: Skill-selection step of a planner over a fixed library of language-labelled skills (551 skills in 7 families; subset used)
signatures.information: LLM sees instruction + already selected skill labels, not the scene; affordance function sees the current image state through the skill's value function; object locations for navigation assumed known (E013)
signatures.operation: for every skill compute p_LLM(label|instruction, history) x p_affordance(success|state); execute argmax; append label; repeat until 'done'
signatures.output: executed sequence of skills with a visible score table per step
signatures.conditions: skills with value functions/heuristic affordances; labels admissible as LLM completions; prompt of 17 dialog examples
signatures.feedback: state-conditioned value only at decision time; no post-execution success check (E017)
signatures.selection_data: no data; prompt designed in a language-based simulator over 50 instructions (E016)
signatures.claimed_effect: plan success 84 vs 67 (No VF) / 74 (Generative); execution 74 mock / 60 real
signatures.failure_boundary: LLM early termination, negation, affordance misclassification (35% of errors), skill capability

signatures.object: Affordance module from value functions and heuristics
signatures.information: RL Q-networks (pick), distance (go-to), constant (place=1.0), small constant (terminate=0.1); completed-skill cap
signatures.operation: normalize/clamp values with empirical constants to [0,1] and treat as success probability
signatures.selection_data: empirical calibration constants, source of tuning data not given
signatures.claimed_effect: world-grounding; embodiment-family plan success 64 vs 18 without it
signatures.failure_boundary: hand-set place/terminate affordances; value function errors

retention_trace.reason: no candidate change is selected/persisted across tasks; skills and prompt are fixed. Adding drawer skills is manual extension (E020)

gap.author_gap: LLMs lack real-world experience, so their plans may not be feasible or contextually appropriate for a given embodiment (spill example)
gap.checked_gap: supported by the paper's own ablations: without the value function plan success falls to 67%, and by state-dependent embodiment instructions 64% vs 18% (E008, E023)

closest_adjacent.note: treated as the Generative baseline; gap: no grounding

lineage.method_note: local texts only; no external search

gap.residue: no recovery from skill failure after a high affordance, LLM early termination, negation, fixed skill library, known object positions, hand-set affordance constants
gap.stakes: makes LLM semantic knowledge usable on a real robot with interpretable, state-aware plans
gap.method_response: state-conditioned value function reweights LLM likelihoods so infeasible but plausible skills are not chosen
gap.remaining_gap: closed-loop feedback and skill capability (E017, E024), and the grounding gain at execution level was not measured because ablations were scored at plan level only
unresolved: whether the value-function gain holds at execution level

tactic_steps_checked: step1 responsibility boundary: executed (LLM proposes/scores; skills+value functions execute and check feasibility)
step2 typed intermediate artifact: executed (skill label from a closed set)
step3 close loop with verifiable output: partial (value function is a learned pre-execution check; no post-execution verdict)
step4 ablate verification step: executed (No VF, Generative)
step5 account for cost: not executed (planning cost unreported; training compute only)
success_failure_checks: learned/solver seam drawn at comparative advantage: met
feedback signals the system can obtain: met (value function)
ablation collapses to named baseline: partial (67/74 plan success, not collapse)
cost of added structure unmeasured: failure present
matches.reason: LLM does language proposal while learned skills and value functions own execution and feasibility; the product score is the load-bearing step, but the checker is a learned proxy, not a sound solver

executes_pattern.reason: typed handoff and ablated verifier-in-loop are executed; verifier is learned, pre-execution only, and costs are not accounted

resolves_problem.reason: plan feasibility improves (84 vs 67/74) but execution gain over ungrounded variants was never measured and 26-40% of real-kitchen executions fail

condition_checks.note: semantic skill vocabulary executed by learned/scripted executors, but executor reliability is the stated bottleneck (E024) and execution reaches 74% / 60%
LLM-size effect shown (PaLM vs FLAN) but harness effect not shown across backbones of different strength
a cheap value-function check gates each proposed skill via soft weighting; removing it is ablated (plan 84 vs 67)
35% of plan errors are affordance misclassification (checker is an imperfect proxy)
gate contribution is isolated at plan level, but not at execution level

revision_proposals.note: K201 is described as dispatch-or-reject with structured feedback; SayCan weights proposals softly by a learned value function and returns no feedback to the model. Suggest noting a soft-gating variant if >=2 independent full-text papers share it (not proposed for now).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: the learned model emits only a label from a closed skill vocabulary and low-level policies execute it, matching C25's confinement of the learned model to the interface artifact and K104's fixed semantic vocabulary over an executor
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K104 requires a reliable executor; here reliability is imperfect and not separately certified; the vocabulary is scored, not freely generated

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: a checker grades each proposal before execution; the learned value function plays the checker role of C25 step3
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K201 expects a checker whose pass condition correlates with success and structured rejection feedback; here soft multiplicative weighting and no post-hoc success check

claims.text: grounding by value functions improves planning over ungrounded LLM planning
claims.baseline_control: No VF (max LLM score) and Generative (LLM decode then USE projection)
claims.selection_vs_test: prompt tuned on language simulator; instruction families designed by authors
claims.result: plan success 84% vs 67% / 74%; embodiment family 64% vs 18% / 36%
counterevidence: 'nearly doubles' (E001) is not supported by aggregate plan success (84 vs 67/74, i.e. 1.1-1.25x); execution of the ablations was not run
BC USE reaches 60% on single primitives

claims.text: SayCan executes long-horizon abstract instructions on a real mobile manipulator
claims.setting: mock kitchen and real kitchen, Everyday Robots, human-rated video
claims.selection_vs_test: skills trained in mock kitchen; screened in real kitchen
claims.allowed_conclusion: moderate execution success on 101 author-designed instructions on one platform

claims.text: better LLMs give better robot performance
claims.setting: PaLM 540B vs FLAN 137B (and sizes at plan level)
counterevidence: PaLM vs FLAN differ in family and data, not just size; 62B vs 540B nearly equal
claims.allowed_conclusion: PaLM outperforms FLAN here; size scaling beyond 62B is not shown to help

assessment.evidence_level_reason: closed-loop real-robot execution with counts per family (101 instructions) judged by human raters; skills trained/screened in the evaluated environments, one embodiment, so not transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2)
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On a mobile manipulator in one office kitchen setup, value-function-weighted LLM skill selection reaches 84% plan and 74% execution success on 101 author-designed single-trial instructions; plan success is higher than without the value function (67%) or with generative projection (74%)
assessment.author_claim_kept: grounding nearly doubles performance over non-grounded baselines
unresolved: execution-level gain of the value function
assessment.reproduction: author-reported only; nothing run by us

G.reason: concrete, important bottleneck with a named nearest neighbor (concurrent Huang et al., tested as the Generative baseline) and clearly stated residue (skill capability, no closed-loop recovery, negation)

M.reason: probabilistic factorization with explicit assumption (failed skill makes zero progress) gives distinguishable predictions, tested by No-VF/Generative; but affordance calibration constants are empirical, place/terminate affordances are hand-set, and the product-of-probabilities reading is not validated

X.reason: Algorithm 1, prompt listing, affordance formulas, skill families and failure modes (LLM early stop, affordance error, skill bottleneck) allow reconstruction; information permissions are explicit (LLM does not see the scene, assumed known object positions); extra hand logic (completion cap) is disclosed

measurement.reason: success criteria and denominators are defined (101 instructions, 3-rater majority for plan and execution) but each instruction is run once, raters are human majority without agreement statistics, and ablations are plan-level only (anchors v2: single trial per item caps at 2)

causality.reason: No-VF, Generative, no-LLM BC and LLM-size/FLAN ablations with the same instructions isolate the grounding and the LLM; however the grounding effect is not measured at execution level, PaLM vs FLAN confounds model family, and the doubling claim is overstated

holdout.reason: mock-kitchen evaluation is the skills' training environment, real-kitchen skills were screened during development, prompt examples resemble evaluation families, one embodiment; real kitchen shows a 14-point execution drop rather than a retained gain

statistics.reason: denominators per family are small (11-15) with one trial per instruction and no variance, but a 65/35 error decomposition and early-termination diagnosis are reported

cost.reason: training compute is disclosed (16 TPUv3 x ~100 h), but planning/inference cost, LLM scoring calls per step and latency are not reported and ablations are not budget-matched
